sdg4.title: What If? — Quality Education (SDG 4)
sdg4.story: After the Storm: Will Every Student Return?
sdg4.disclaimer: Luma and its characters are fictional; the emergency and education barriers are based on documented real-world risks.

intro.scene: A flooded rural school as storm clouds clear. Students and teachers wait at a temporary shelter.
intro.title: After the Storm
intro.text: You are the president of Luma, responsible for the emergency education recovery plan. A severe storm has damaged schools, roads and electricity in rural districts. The storm has passed, but thousands of students cannot return to class. Your first decisions will shape the recovery.

choices.label: START THE STORY

n1.scene: Emergency cabinet room with a map showing urban and rural school damage.
n1.title: Emergency budget
n1.text: The emergency budget cannot immediately fund every repair. Equitable allocation considers need, not only the number of buildings.

choices.label: Repair the largest urban schools first
choices.consequence: More students may return quickly in dense areas, but isolated rural communities stay without nearby classrooms and transport, and trust in the plan falls in remote areas.

choices.label: Prioritize the most isolated and vulnerable communities
choices.consequence: Fewer students return immediately, but remote learners are less likely to be left behind. Urban repairs proceed in phases.

n2a.scene: A crowded urban gym used as a temporary classroom. The rural school is still out of reach.
n2a.title: Temporary learning
n2a.text: Families demand immediate lessons while repairs continue.

choices.label: Use one large temporary learning center only
choices.consequence: Some students receive lessons, but transport, disability access and distance keep others from attending.

choices.label: Create several small community learning spaces and mobile teaching teams
choices.consequence: Coverage improves across neighborhoods, but coordination and teacher scheduling become harder.

n2b.scene: A rural community hall with teachers, families and students.
n2b.title: Teachers and student support
n2b.text: Buildings are being repaired, but some teachers have lost housing and students lack books, devices or transport.

choices.label: Spend most remaining funds on devices and online classes
choices.consequence: Connected students can keep learning, but communities without reliable electricity or internet are excluded.

choices.label: Fund teacher support, printed learning kits, transport and safe temporary spaces
choices.consequence: More learners can take part offline and teachers can return, while advanced digital access develops more slowly.

n3a.scene: A school gate reopening, with a long queue of students.
n3a.title: Reopening plan
n3a.text: Repairs are nearly done. How should schools reopen?

choices.label: A rapid reopening with limited support
choices.consequence: Doors open fast, but there is little support for students who fell behind.

choices.label: A phased reopening with teacher training, accessible materials and learning assessments
choices.consequence: Reopening is slower, but teachers are trained and learning is checked.

n3b.scene: Small learning spaces across several neighborhoods.
n3b.title: Reopening plan
n3b.text: Repairs are nearly done. How should schools reopen?

choices.label: A rapid reopening with limited support
choices.consequence: Doors open fast, but there is little support for students who fell behind.

choices.label: A phased reopening with teacher training, accessible materials and learning assessments
choices.consequence: Reopening is slower, but teachers are trained and learning is checked.

n3c.scene: A dashboard of reopened buildings, with blank spaces for disconnected districts.
n3c.title: How will you measure success?
n3c.text: The online plan is running. What counts as success?

choices.label: Count only the buildings reopened
choices.consequence: Progress looks good on paper, while disconnected students are not tracked.

choices.label: Also track attendance, learning recovery and participation of remote and disadvantaged students
choices.consequence: You see the gaps, but the online-first plan makes them hard to close.

n3d.scene: Printed learning kits and a progress board in a rural school.
n3d.title: How will you measure success?
n3d.text: Offline support is working. What counts as success?

choices.label: Count only the buildings reopened
choices.consequence: Schools reopen, but access gaps stay hidden.

choices.label: Also track attendance, learning recovery and participation of remote and disadvantaged students
choices.consequence: You can see who is returning and who still needs help.

end1.title: Reopened, but not for everyone
end1.text: Buildings reopen but access gaps remain.

end2.scene: Students of different ages and abilities learning together.
end2.title: A connected recovery
end2.text: Schools reopen with resilient plans, teacher support and inclusive access.

end3.scene: A dark classroom while screens glow elsewhere.
end3.title: Lessons interrupted again
end3.text: Online-only planning leaves disconnected students behind.

sdg4.takeaway: SDG 4 requires equitable access, actual learning, safe facilities and qualified teachers, not just reopened buildings.

sdg5.title: What If? — Gender Equality (SDG 5)
sdg5.story: A Seat at the Table: Who Shapes the Recovery?
sdg5.disclaimer: Solana and its characters are fictional; the story is evidence-informed and educational.

intro.scene: A community meeting where only a few voices are heard, while women wait outside with practical knowledge and proposals.
intro.title: A Seat at the Table
intro.text: You are head of the recovery council in Solana, a coastal community rebuilding after a major emergency. The council decides on safety, housing, jobs and public resources, but women and girls are being left out of important meetings. The community must rebuild. But can a recovery plan be fair if half the community is not heard?

choices.label: START THE STORY

n1.scene: The recovery council chamber, with the community waiting outside.
n1.title: Who is on the council?
n1.text: Urgent decisions are being made, but women and girls have no meaningful representation. Participation means influence, not a symbolic seat.

choices.label: Keep the existing council to make decisions faster
choices.consequence: Decisions may come quickly, but they risk overlooking the safety, care, livelihood and access needs of excluded residents.

choices.label: Create an inclusive council with meaningful participation by women and affected groups
choices.consequence: More perspectives shape the plan, although consultation and transparent decision-making take time.

n2a.scene: A temporary shelter entrance and a public service desk.
n2a.title: Safety and protection
n2a.text: Reports show that some residents do not feel safe using temporary shelters and services.

choices.label: Treat safety as an individual issue and keep current arrangements
choices.consequence: Barriers may stay unreported and some residents avoid services.

choices.label: Consult affected residents and set up confidential reporting, trained staff and safe access procedures
choices.consequence: Reporting and access may improve, but staff training, privacy and follow-up resources are needed.

n2b.scene: A reconstruction job fair and a distribution center.
n2b.title: Resources and opportunity
n2b.text: Paid reconstruction jobs, grants and equipment are being shared through informal networks that may exclude women.

choices.label: Distribute opportunities through existing informal contacts
choices.consequence: Resources may reach familiar groups quickly, but access can stay unequal and opaque.

choices.label: Publish transparent eligibility rules and ensure equal access to jobs, grants and services
choices.consequence: Decisions become more accountable and access can widen, while outreach and monitoring are needed to reach excluded residents.

n3a.scene: A closing report on the recovery.
n3a.title: After the first response
n3a.text: The emergency phase is ending. What happens next?

choices.label: Fund ongoing prevention, confidential support and accountability mechanisms
choices.consequence: Safety becomes part of the recovery system.

choices.label: Treat the initial response as complete
choices.consequence: Gaps stay in place once attention moves on.

n3b.scene: A closing report on the recovery.
n3b.title: After the first response
n3b.text: The emergency phase is ending. What happens next?

choices.label: Fund ongoing prevention, confidential support and accountability mechanisms
choices.consequence: Safety becomes part of the recovery system.

choices.label: Treat the initial response as complete
choices.consequence: The consultation happened, but nothing keeps it going.

n3c.scene: A ledger of aid, with a column for who received it left empty.
n3c.title: How will you measure fairness?
n3c.text: Aid is flowing. How will you judge the result?

choices.label: Measure only the amount of aid distributed
choices.consequence: The totals look strong, and the exclusion goes unseen.

choices.label: Also examine who received it, who participated and whether access was fair
choices.consequence: You find the gaps, but nothing requires anyone to fix them.

n3d.scene: A public board showing who received jobs and grants.
n3d.title: How will you measure fairness?
n3d.text: Transparent rules are in place. How will you judge the result?

choices.label: Measure only the amount of aid distributed
choices.consequence: Rules were published, but without monitoring they are not followed through.

choices.label: Also examine who received it, who participated and whether access was fair
choices.consequence: You can see who gained access and act where it falls short.

end1.scene: Rebuilt streets with half the community missing from view.
end1.title: Rebuilding without every voice

end2.scene: A neighborhood meeting where women lead alongside others.
end2.title: Shared leadership, stronger recovery
end2.text: Participation, safety and transparent access become part of the recovery system.

end3.scene: A signed plan with no budget attached.
end3.title: Promises without follow-through
end3.text: Inclusive meetings take place, but no budget, accountability or implementation follows.

sdg5.takeaway: SDG 5 requires rights, safety, equal opportunity, shared responsibility and meaningful leadership.
